chosen.title: The Factory That Forms Metal by Hand: Inside the Robotic Craftsmen Reshaping Aerospace Manufacturing
chosen.rationale: Machina Labs just opened a 200,000 sq-ft 'physical AI' factory where two-armed robots use real-time AI to shape titanium and aluminum aerospace parts in days instead of months — backed by a fresh $124M round with Toyota and Lockheed Martin. It's a perfect Kenji story: a tangible mechanism (robots literally hammering metal into shape), a maker's sense of wonder, and honest stakes about labor and defense.

rejected_candidates.title: The Weather Machine Learned to Guess: How AI Forecasts Now See 45 Days Into the Sky
rejected_candidates.rationale: NOAA just put a new generation of AI-driven global weather models into operation, and systems like DeepMet are pushing accurate long-range forecasts out to 45 days while using a fraction of the compute — cutting error 20-60% versus the leading physics model. This lands squarely in Kenji's climate-tech and 'planet as a character' territory, with a clean mechanism to explain and real stakes for extreme-heat warning.

rejected_candidates.title: Teaching Robots to Move in Zero Gravity: How AI Path-Planning Is Rewiring Work in Orbit
rejected_candidates.rationale: NASA is now using AI-enabled 'warm start' motion planning to speed up ISS robot path-planning by 50-60%, while labs push dexterous multi-fingered manipulation for unstructured environments. It's an aerospace-meets-robotics story with a vivid physical hook — a robot learning to reach for a bolt in freefall — that fits Kenji's window-seat-with-a-research-paper enthusiasm perfectly.
